newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 28.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

RTZ-CRA has demanded an improvement in efficiency to world best standards from its Australian subsidiaries, Comalco and Coal & Allied, as a condition of its continued support of the troubled organisations. The world's biggest mining company announced yesterday a fall in net profit to A$1.4 billion in 1996 due to lower metal prices and fluctuations in exchange rates. Page 1.

Mayne Nickless Ltd is still set to sell its 25 percent stake in Optus despite abandoning plans to float its holdings on the sharemarket. The company needs to offload its Optus stake to finance its further growth plans. One option it is now considering s making a free issue of its Optus shares to its stockholders. Page 33.

Mayne Nickless has announced a 13.8 percent fall in interim net profit to A$43.14 million and is now hoping for improved second-half earnings. Managing Director Bob Dalziel said the result was in line with company expectations and reflected the restructring of Mayne's European and Australian interests. Page 33.

Gold mining company Newcrest is hoping that its shares in Normandy Mining will rise against the world gold price over the next two years to reduce the massive losses it has already suffered from its 11.9 per cent stake. Page 34.

Aristocrat Leisure Ltd yesterday announced that it expects to meet its prospectus forecast but only because the New South Wales government has decided to allow pubs to install poker machines. The decision means that from April 1 pubs will be able to increase their "card" machines from 10 to 15 and install an additional 15 club-type poker machines. Page 35.

Tabcorp Holdings chief executive Ross Wilson declared yesterday that restructuring of the formerly Victorian Government owned TAB was now complete. The announcement followed an improvement in interim net profits by 17.5 percent. Wilson indicated that Tabcorp remained interested in buying into the New South Wales TAB, although the state government was yet to release plans on privatisation. Page 25.

NRMA has announced a net profit of A$229.4 million for the six months to December 31. The chief executive of NRMA Malcolm Jones was confident that the second half of the financial year would see increasing profits and credited the results to good planning and leadership at the board level. Page 37.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Mining giant RTZ-CRA last night announced its annual result had dropped 24 percent to A$1.403 billion from A$1.736 billion as depressed metals prices and a higher Australian dollar took its toll on the bottom line. The world's biggest miner said its key copper and aluminium operations in Australia and the U.S. had also been hit hard. Page 21.

Pay TV group Optus Vision sustained losses of A$168.2 million in the six months to December as its capitalisation programme continued. This latest result, revealed in the interim results of shareholder Mayne Nickless, indicates total losses for the Australian pay TV industry will approach A$1.5 billion this financial year. Page 21.

Two senior executives have resigned from mining group MIM Holdings as major reforms in the company's management structure continues. The departing executive general managers are exploration boss Dr Ross Fardon and metals division chief Geoff Billard. It is believed the two resigned in the wake of major reforms implemented by recently appointed MIM managing director Nick Stump. Page 21.

Mayne Nickless Ltd has abandoned its A$1 billion float of its 25 percent share holdings in Optus Communications, and is planning other options to dispose of its stake in the telecommunications company before the end of the financial year. The legal probems surrounding Optus Vision, a subsidiary of Optus, had prevented the float. Page 23.

National Mutual Ltd is hoping to win a life insurance licence in China to operate in one province, managing director Geoff Tomlinson said yesterday. Speaking at a Melbourne Asia-link seminar he outlined that if successful the company would have to commit a modest A$40 million of capital to the project. Page 22.

The latest federal figures reveal that resource investment has increased heavily in the last 12 months with A$5.4 billion in projects being completed. Analysts predict that the whole sector will experience an investment boom with over A$55 bilion in new projects either committed or being planned. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As the saga of the two miners continues, Newcrest Mining has cashed in its 11.9 percent stake in Normandy Mining in an equity gold swap leaving Newcrest with a A$134.7 million loss on the investment. The deal took centre stage over Newcrest's posting of a profit before abnormals of A$6.3 million for the December half. Page 27.

Mayne Nickless has announced that it will sell its 25 percent in Optus Communications by mid-March for between A$700 million and A$1 billion to provide firepower for a A$2 billion bid for Europe's largest private hospital operator, Generale de Sante. Pag 27

NRMA Group has announced a A$229.4 million profit in the December half-year which has been powered by higher income and capital gains from its investment portfolio and overall improved results from its insurance operations. The profit was a major increase on the A$85.4 million for the previous December half. Page 29.

Increased gaming revenues and lower operations costs have assisted a 17.5 percent increase in the Victorian-based Tabcorp's interim net profits to A$51.21 million. The cashed up Tabcorp is now in a position to make a bid for the New South Wales Totalisator Agency Board (NSW TAB) when it is eventually privatised for an estimated A$1 billion. Page 29.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has expressed concerned about becoming the media regulator under the Federal Government's planned new media regime. ACCC chairman Alan Fels told a conference in Sydney that the industry watchdog is "not necessarily very interested" in taking on the new role. Page 31.

According to figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics, business investment fell 2.4 percent to A$7.2 billion in the December quarter. The figure threatens the government's economic growth forecasts. However, analysts expect investment to pick up strongly over the next year. Page 31.
THE AGE

The world's biggest mining company, RTZ-CRA has taken a beating on the profit line as a result of fallout from the Sumitomo copper scandal, shortcomings at Comalco and its U.S. copper operations. Full-year 1996 profit for the giant had fell 24 percent to A$1.4 billion despite substantial across-the-board increases in production. Page B1.

Mayne Nickless will finalise a plan to offload its 25 percent stake in Optus Communications by mid-March. Mayne hopes the sale will provide backing for a planned A$2 billion bid for Europe's largest private hospital operator, Generale de Sante. Yesterday Mayne posted a 13.8 percent slump in net profit to A$44.1 million for the six months to December. Page B1.

According to notes in Mayne Nickless accounts, the pay TV and telephony group Optus Vision lost A$168.2 million in the six months to December. The figure is expected to increase as the group continues its A$3 billion installation of overhead cabling. Mayne Nickless has an 11.6 percent indirect stake in Optus Vision. Page B1.

The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group is struggling to control costs as indicated by the first-quarter report from its New Zealand operation which reveals a decline in the key cost-to-income ratio. ANZ New Zealand announced a NZ$30.1 million profit for the December quarter which is down from NZ$36.9 million for the previous corresponding period. The New Zealand division is the only part of the bank legally required to report quarterly figures. Page B3.

BankWest is among the increasing number of regional banks which are being pressured by reduced interest-rate margins on home lending. It announced yesterday that its full year profit will fail to meet the prospectus forecast of A$100.2 million by about five per cent. The bank's chairman Ian Mackenzie also warned there would be a further decline in profits for the coming year due to continuing home-loan interest-rate cuts. Page B3.

The growth of Victoria's gambling industry this year was reflected in the 17.5 percent rise in Tabcorp's interim net profit to A$51.2 million. Lying behind the result is a surge in gaming revenues and lower costs in both wagering and gaming operations. The profit surge has put Tabcorp into a strong position to bid for the New South Wales Totalisator Agency Board when it is privatised. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
